name: JavaScript & TypeScript
description: Async code that works until it doesn't, and the types that catch it before production.

concepts.name: Event loop
concepts.description: The call stack runs to completion; then microtasks (promise callbacks) drain before the next macrotask (timers, I/O).

concepts.name: Promises
concepts.description: A promise is a placeholder for a future value; then/catch callbacks run as microtasks and chains pass values along.

concepts.name: async/await
concepts.description: await pauses only the async function, not the thread; every async function returns a promise.

concepts.name: Closures
concepts.description: A function keeps access to the variables of the scope where it was created, even after that scope has returned.

concepts.name: this binding
concepts.description: this is decided by how a function is called, not where it is written; arrow functions take this from the enclosing scope.

concepts.name: == vs ===
concepts.description: === compares without type conversion; == converts types first, which produces surprising results.

concepts.name: Mutation vs copy
concepts.description: Objects and arrays are passed by reference; spreading copies only one level deep.

concepts.name: Hoisting
concepts.description: var and function declarations are hoisted; let and const are hoisted too but unusable before their line (temporal dead zone).

concepts.name: var, let and const
concepts.description: var is function-scoped, let and const are block-scoped; const forbids reassignment, not mutation.

concepts.name: Array methods
concepts.description: map, filter and reduce return new values; sort and splice mutate in place, and sort compares strings by default.

concepts.name: Types and coercion
concepts.description: typeof, truthy and falsy values, and the implicit conversions JavaScript performs with + and comparisons.

concepts.name: Error handling
concepts.description: try/catch only catches what is thrown synchronously or awaited; an unawaited rejected promise escapes it.

concepts.name: Types and interfaces
concepts.description: TypeScript checks shapes at compile time and erases them at runtime; interfaces and type aliases both describe object shapes.

concepts.name: Narrowing
concepts.description: typeof, in, equality checks and discriminant fields narrow a union to one member inside a branch.

concepts.name: Generics
concepts.description: A generic keeps the link between input and output types instead of falling back to any.

concepts.name: any, unknown and never
concepts.description: any switches checking off, unknown forces a check before use, never marks what cannot happen.

name: Frontend
description: Components that render forty times: the browser and framework mechanics behind a UI.

concepts.name: Semantic HTML
concepts.description: Elements such as button, nav, main and label carry meaning that browsers, search engines and screen readers rely on.

concepts.name: Box model
concepts.description: Every element is content, padding, border and margin; box-sizing decides whether width includes padding and border.

concepts.name: CSS specificity
concepts.description: IDs beat classes, classes beat elements; later rules win ties, and !important overrides the normal order.

concepts.name: Flexbox and grid
concepts.description: Flexbox lays out one dimension, grid two; both replace float and table layout hacks.

concepts.name: Responsive design
concepts.description: Fluid layouts, relative units and media queries adapt one page to every screen; mobile-first starts from the smallest.

concepts.name: DOM and reflow
concepts.description: Reading layout after writing styles forces the browser to recalculate layout synchronously.

concepts.name: Events and delegation
concepts.description: Events bubble from the target up through its ancestors, so one listener on a parent can handle many children.

concepts.name: State and re-render
concepts.description: A component re-renders when its state or props change; derived values should be computed, not stored.

concepts.name: Effects and dependencies
concepts.description: An effect runs after render and re-runs when a listed dependency changes; a missing dependency reads stale values.

concepts.name: Keys in lists
concepts.description: A stable key lets the framework match list items between renders; an index as key breaks when items move.

concepts.name: Memo and lazy loading
concepts.description: Memoization skips repeated work; lazy loading defers code until it is needed.

concepts.name: Accessibility
concepts.description: Semantic elements, labels and keyboard focus make an interface usable with assistive technology.

name: Backend & APIs
description: Endpoints without validation and layers without purpose: how a server should behave.

concepts.name: HTTP semantics and status codes
concepts.description: Methods carry meaning (safe, idempotent) and status codes tell the client what happened.

concepts.name: REST design
concepts.description: Resources are nouns in URLs; the method says what to do with them.

concepts.name: Validation
concepts.description: Validate every input at the boundary and reject it with a clear 400 before any work happens.

concepts.name: Error handling
concepts.description: Return consistent error bodies and never leak stack traces or internal messages to clients.

concepts.name: Authentication flow
concepts.description: Authentication proves who you are; authorization decides what you may do.

concepts.name: Middleware
concepts.description: Middleware runs in order around every request; its position in the pipeline matters.

concepts.name: Idempotency
concepts.description: Repeating an idempotent request has the same effect as sending it once; retries rely on it.

concepts.name: Pagination
concepts.description: Large lists come in pages; cursor pagination stays correct while rows are inserted, offset pagination does not.

concepts.name: Rate limiting
concepts.description: Limiting requests per client protects the server from abuse; the client gets 429 and Retry-After.

concepts.name: Server-side caching
concepts.description: A cache keeps computed results close by; every cached value needs a rule for when it becomes stale.

concepts.name: Background jobs
concepts.description: Slow work such as e-mail or image processing moves to a queue so the request can answer quickly.

concepts.name: Coupling
concepts.description: Modules that know too much about each other change together; dependencies should point inward.

name: Databases & SQL
description: The query that works on a hundred rows and dies on a million.

concepts.name: JOIN types
concepts.description: INNER JOIN keeps matching rows only; LEFT JOIN keeps every left row and fills missing right columns with NULL.

concepts.name: Indexes
concepts.description: An index turns a full table scan into a lookup, at the cost of slower writes and extra storage.

concepts.name: N+1 queries
concepts.description: Loading a list and then querying once per item sends N+1 queries where one join or batch would do.

concepts.name: Transactions and ACID
concepts.description: A transaction makes several statements succeed or fail together.

concepts.name: Normalization
concepts.description: Store each fact once; duplicated data drifts apart when only one copy is updated.

concepts.name: NULL semantics
concepts.description: NULL means unknown: comparisons with NULL are neither true nor false, so use IS NULL.

concepts.name: GROUP BY and HAVING
concepts.description: GROUP BY collapses rows into groups; WHERE filters rows before grouping, HAVING filters groups after.

concepts.name: Subqueries
concepts.description: A subquery can produce a value, a list for IN, or a table; EXISTS stops at the first match.

concepts.name: Keys and constraints
concepts.description: Primary keys, foreign keys, UNIQUE and CHECK let the database reject bad data itself.

concepts.name: Isolation and locking
concepts.description: Concurrent transactions can see each other's changes depending on the isolation level; locks prevent lost updates.

concepts.name: Logical query order
concepts.description: SQL runs FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT, in that order, not as written.

concepts.name: Views
concepts.description: A view is a stored query used like a table; it holds no data unless it is materialized.

name: Networking & web
description: The CORS error that goes straight into ChatGPT: what happens between browser and server.

concepts.name: IP addresses and ports
concepts.description: An IP address finds the machine, a port finds the program on it; localhost is the machine itself.

concepts.name: TCP vs UDP
concepts.description: TCP delivers ordered, reliable streams; UDP sends independent packets with no delivery guarantee.

concepts.name: DNS
concepts.description: DNS translates names into IP addresses through a chain of cached lookups.

concepts.name: URLs
concepts.description: A URL is scheme, host, port, path, query and fragment; the fragment never reaches the server.

concepts.name: HTTP requests and responses
concepts.description: A request is a method, a path, headers and an optional body; a response is a status code, headers and a body.

concepts.name: HTTP caching
concepts.description: Cache-Control and validators such as ETag decide who may reuse a response and for how long.

concepts.name: Cookies
concepts.description: The server sets cookies and the browser sends them back on matching requests; flags limit where they go.

concepts.name: CORS
concepts.description: The browser blocks reading cross-origin responses unless the server allows the origin.

concepts.name: TLS
concepts.description: TLS encrypts the connection and proves the server's identity with a certificate.

concepts.name: WebSocket vs HTTP
concepts.description: WebSocket keeps one connection open for messages in both directions; HTTP is request and response.

concepts.name: Proxies and load balancers
concepts.description: A reverse proxy sits in front of servers to terminate TLS, route and balance load; the client only sees the proxy.

concepts.name: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3
concepts.description: HTTP/2 multiplexes many requests over one connection; HTTP/3 runs over QUIC on UDP.

name: Cybersecurity
description: AI writes vulnerable code and nobody reads it: the mistakes attackers look for first.

concepts.name: SQL injection
concepts.description: Concatenating input into SQL lets it become code; parameters keep data as data.

concepts.name: XSS
concepts.description: Inserting untrusted text into HTML without escaping lets it run as script in other users' browsers.

concepts.name: CSRF
concepts.description: A forged request from another site rides on the victim's cookies unless the server checks its origin.

concepts.name: Broken access control
concepts.description: Checking that a user is logged in is not enough; every request must check that this user may touch this resource.

concepts.name: Hashing vs encryption
concepts.description: Encryption is reversible with a key; password hashing is one-way and deliberately slow.

concepts.name: Secrets in code
concepts.description: Keys committed to a repository are public forever; load them from the environment.

concepts.name: JWT pitfalls
concepts.description: A JWT is signed, not encrypted; the server must verify the signature, algorithm and expiry.

concepts.name: Input validation
concepts.description: Validate on the server with allow-lists; client-side checks are a convenience, not protection.

concepts.name: Session cookies
concepts.description: HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite keep session cookies away from scripts, plain HTTP and other sites.

concepts.name: SSRF
concepts.description: A server that fetches user-supplied URLs can be pointed at internal services and cloud metadata.

concepts.name: Dependencies and supply chain
concepts.description: Every package you install runs with your permissions; pin versions and update known-vulnerable ones.

concepts.name: Least privilege
concepts.description: Give each user, service and key only the permissions it needs, so a leak does limited damage.

name: Algorithms & data structures
description: It works, but it's O(n²): choosing the structure that keeps code fast.

concepts.name: Complexity
concepts.description: Big O describes how work grows with input size; nested loops over the same data are usually O(n²).

concepts.name: Hash map vs list
concepts.description: A hash map finds a key in constant time on average; searching a list is linear.

concepts.name: Stack and queue
concepts.description: A stack is last in, first out; a queue is first in, first out.

concepts.name: Linked lists
concepts.description: A linked list inserts and removes in constant time at a known node but must walk the list to find an index.

concepts.name: Recursion
concepts.description: A recursive function needs a base case; each call uses stack space until it returns.

concepts.name: Sorting
concepts.description: Good general sorts are O(n log n); a stable sort keeps the order of equal elements.

concepts.name: Binary search
concepts.description: On sorted data, halving the search range each step finds an item in O(log n).

concepts.name: Two pointers and sliding window
concepts.description: Two indexes moving through an array solve many pair and subarray problems in one pass.

concepts.name: Trees
concepts.description: A binary search tree keeps smaller keys left and larger right; its speed depends on staying balanced.

concepts.name: Heaps and priority queues
concepts.description: A heap returns the smallest (or largest) item in O(log n) per removal, which is what a priority queue needs.

concepts.name: BFS and DFS
concepts.description: Breadth-first search explores level by level with a queue; depth-first goes deep with a stack.

concepts.name: Dynamic programming
concepts.description: When subproblems repeat, storing their answers turns exponential recursion into polynomial work.

name: Git & version control
description: The force push that erased a week of work: how Git actually stores and moves history.

concepts.name: Commits and the staging area
concepts.description: git add puts changes in the staging area; a commit records a snapshot of exactly what was staged.

concepts.name: Branches and HEAD
concepts.description: A branch is a movable pointer to a commit; HEAD points to what you have checked out.

concepts.name: Merging
concepts.description: A merge joins two histories; it fast-forwards when one side has no new commits, otherwise it creates a merge commit.

concepts.name: Rebasing
concepts.description: Rebase replays commits on a new base, creating new commits; never rebase history others have pulled.

concepts.name: Merge conflicts
concepts.description: A conflict appears when both sides changed the same lines; you edit the file, remove the markers and stage it.

concepts.name: Remotes: fetch, pull and push
concepts.description: fetch downloads remote commits, pull is fetch plus merge (or rebase), push uploads and is rejected when you are behind.

concepts.name: Undoing changes
concepts.description: restore discards working changes, reset moves the branch pointer, revert adds a commit that undoes another.

concepts.name: Reading history
concepts.description: log, diff, show and blame answer what changed, when and by whom; bisect finds the commit that broke something.

concepts.name: Stash
concepts.description: stash shelves uncommitted changes so you can switch branches and bring them back later.

concepts.name: .gitignore
concepts.description: .gitignore keeps untracked files out of Git; a file that is already tracked stays tracked until you remove it from the index.

concepts.name: Branching workflow and pull requests
concepts.description: Short-lived feature branches merged through reviewed pull requests keep the main branch releasable.

concepts.name: Tags and releases
concepts.description: A tag names a specific commit, usually a release version; unlike a branch it does not move.

name: OS & Linux
description: Permission denied, port already in use: the operating system under every server.

concepts.name: Processes
concepts.description: A process is a running program with its own memory and PID; a parent starts children and collects their exit status.

concepts.name: Threads and concurrency
concepts.description: Threads share their process's memory, so unsynchronized writes to shared data cause race conditions.

concepts.name: Memory: stack, heap and virtual memory
concepts.description: Each process sees its own virtual address space; the stack holds call frames, the heap holds dynamic allocations.

concepts.name: Filesystem and paths
concepts.description: Everything hangs off / ; absolute paths start there, relative paths start from the current directory.

concepts.name: Permissions
concepts.description: Read, write and execute bits for owner, group and others decide who may do what with a file.

concepts.name: Users and sudo
concepts.description: root can do anything; sudo runs a single command with elevated rights instead of working as root.

concepts.name: Pipes and redirection
concepts.description: | sends one command's output into the next; > and >> redirect output to files, 2> redirects errors.

concepts.name: Text tools
concepts.description: grep finds lines, sort and uniq count them, find locates files, and small tools combine into pipelines.

concepts.name: Environment variables
concepts.description: Environment variables are passed from a process to its children; export makes a shell variable part of it.

concepts.name: Signals and killing processes
concepts.description: SIGTERM asks a process to stop and can be handled; SIGKILL cannot be caught or ignored.

concepts.name: Exit codes
concepts.description: Exit code 0 means success and anything else failure; && and || in the shell branch on it.

concepts.name: Services and logs
concepts.description: systemd starts, restarts and supervises long-running services; journalctl shows their logs.

name: Testing & debugging
description: Green on my machine, red in CI: writing tests that catch bugs and finding the ones they missed.

concepts.name: Unit vs integration tests
concepts.description: A unit test checks one piece in isolation; an integration test checks that pieces work together with real dependencies.

concepts.name: Test pyramid
concepts.description: Many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests and a handful of end-to-end tests keep a suite fast and trustworthy.

concepts.name: Assertions
concepts.description: A test without a meaningful assertion passes no matter what the code does.

concepts.name: Edge cases and boundaries
concepts.description: Bugs gather at boundaries: empty input, zero, one, the maximum, off-by-one limits and invalid values.

concepts.name: Mocks, stubs and fakes
concepts.description: Test doubles replace slow or external dependencies; mocking too much tests the mocks instead of the code.

concepts.name: Test isolation and fixtures
concepts.description: Each test sets up its own state and must pass alone and in any order.

concepts.name: Flaky tests
concepts.description: A flaky test passes and fails without code changes, usually because of time, randomness, order or shared state.

concepts.name: Test-driven development
concepts.description: Write a failing test, make it pass with the simplest code, then refactor with the test as a safety net.

concepts.name: Coverage
concepts.description: Coverage shows which lines ran during tests, not whether their behaviour was checked.

concepts.name: End-to-end tests
concepts.description: End-to-end tests drive the real application like a user; they catch wiring bugs but are slow and brittle.

concepts.name: Debugging method
concepts.description: Reproduce, isolate, form a hypothesis, test it; bisecting the input or the history narrows a bug fast.

concepts.name: Logs and stack traces
concepts.description: A stack trace shows where an exception was thrown and how the code got there; read it from the top frame of your own code.

name: DevOps & cloud basics
description: It works on my machine, so ship the machine: building, shipping and running software.

concepts.name: CI/CD pipelines
concepts.description: Continuous integration builds and tests every change; continuous delivery deploys what passed, automatically.

concepts.name: Containers vs virtual machines
concepts.description: A container packages an app with its dependencies and shares the host kernel; a VM runs a whole guest OS.

concepts.name: Dockerfiles and image layers
concepts.description: Each Dockerfile instruction creates a cached layer; order instructions from least to most frequently changing.

concepts.name: Docker Compose
concepts.description: Compose starts several containers with their networks, volumes and environment from one file.

concepts.name: Volumes and state
concepts.description: A container's filesystem is thrown away with it; data that must survive lives in a volume or a database.

concepts.name: Configuration and environments
concepts.description: The same build runs everywhere; what differs between environments comes from environment variables or config, not code.

concepts.name: Health checks
concepts.description: Liveness says the process is alive, readiness says it can take traffic; orchestrators restart or route by them.

concepts.name: Logs, metrics and traces
concepts.description: Logs say what happened, metrics show trends and alert, traces follow one request across services.

concepts.name: Deployment strategies
concepts.description: Rolling, blue-green and canary deployments replace a version without downtime and allow a fast rollback.

concepts.name: Scaling
concepts.description: Vertical scaling buys a bigger machine, horizontal scaling adds more; autoscaling adds and removes them by load.

concepts.name: Cloud service models
concepts.description: IaaS rents machines, PaaS runs your app, SaaS is finished software, serverless runs functions on demand.

concepts.name: Infrastructure as code
concepts.description: Servers, networks and permissions described in versioned files can be reviewed, repeated and rebuilt.

name: System design basics
description: One server is fine until it isn't: the building blocks of systems that grow.

concepts.name: Requirements and trade-offs
concepts.description: Functional requirements say what the system does; non-functional ones (latency, availability, cost) shape how it is built.

concepts.name: Back-of-the-envelope estimates
concepts.description: Rough numbers for users, requests per second and storage show early which parts must scale.

concepts.name: Stateless services
concepts.description: A server that keeps no session state can be copied freely behind a load balancer.

concepts.name: Load balancing
concepts.description: A load balancer spreads requests over healthy servers using round robin, least connections or hashing.

concepts.name: Caching strategies
concepts.description: Cache-aside, write-through and TTLs trade freshness for speed; invalidation is the hard part.

concepts.name: CDN
concepts.description: A CDN serves static content from servers close to users and takes load off the origin.

concepts.name: Database replication
concepts.description: Read replicas copy the primary to spread reads; replication lag means a replica can return stale data.

concepts.name: Partitioning and sharding
concepts.description: Sharding splits data across databases by a key; a bad key creates hot shards and cross-shard queries.

concepts.name: Message queues
concepts.description: A queue decouples producers from consumers, absorbs spikes and lets work be retried.

concepts.name: Consistency and CAP
concepts.description: During a network partition a distributed system must choose between consistency and availability.

concepts.name: Availability and failure
concepts.description: Redundancy removes single points of failure; 99.9 % uptime still allows almost nine hours of downtime a year.

concepts.name: Monolith vs microservices
concepts.description: Microservices scale teams and parts independently at the cost of network calls, deployment and debugging complexity.
